Chapter 3 · Education, culture and agency

The Sociology of Education · 3.2

Education, culture and agency

教育、文化与能动性

p. 137

The relationship between education and culture cannot be understood as a simple process of transmission. Educational institutions do more than pass established knowledge from one generation to the next; they also create the conditions in which learners may reinterpret, contest, and transform what they inherit.

教育与文化之间的关系不能被理解为一个简单的传递过程。教育机构所做的不仅是把既有知识从一代传给下一代；它们也创造了条件，使学习者能够重新诠释、质疑并转化自己所继承的内容。

This is why the concept of agency has become so substantial in contemporary educational theory. It directs attention to the capacity of individuals to act purposefully within social and institutional constraints, rather than imagining them as merely passive recipients of culture.

这正是“能动性”这一概念在当代教育理论中变得如此重要的原因。它将注意力引向个体在社会和制度约束中有目的地行动的能力，而不是把他们想象成文化的被动接受者。
“Education is never neutral: it names both the reproduction of a world and the possibility of remaking it.”
— Reading note, Chapter 3

A pedagogy that takes agency seriously must therefore make room for dialogue, uncertainty, and reflection. The teacher does not withdraw from responsibility; instead, the teacher provides scaffolding through which students can gradually take greater ownership of their learning.

因此，认真对待能动性的教学法必须为对话、不确定性和反思留出空间。教师并非放弃责任；相反，教师提供支架，使学生能够逐步对自己的学习承担更多主体责任。
p. 138

The distinction is far more complicated than it initially appears. Cultural resources are unequally distributed, and the ability to use them is shaped by prior experience. Yet this does not mean that educational action is predetermined. It means that good teaching must attend to the particular histories and possibilities that students bring into the classroom.

这种区分远比最初看起来复杂。文化资源的分配并不均等，而使用这些资源的能力又受到既往经验塑造。但这并不意味着教育行动已被预先决定；它意味着，好的教学必须关注学生带入课堂的具体经历与可能性。
